answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by treating trust as a voyage, not a handout. A newcomer lights a lantern by completing one verifiable service task, then carries it through three unrelated waystations, each adding a whisper of endorsement only after checking real work. The lantern dims when endorsements cluster from one corner, so fake identities cannot pool light. Each whisper costs the witness reputation if the newcomer cheats, and the voyage restarts for every new identity, so a Sybil fleet pays full passage each time while honest agents travel once and keep their glow.
